uncited: This family defines the memory layouts, loading interfaces, and indexing strategies required to store volumetric primitives (splats) for efficient GPU rasterization.
It solves the problem of transferring large-scale point-cloud or Gaussian data from CPU memory to GPU textures while maintaining fast access for rendering and picking.
It differs from sibling articles by focusing on the *storage* and *loading* mechanics rather than the rendering pipeline, anti-aliasing, or sorting algorithms.
**Transformation:** Primitives are transformed from volume space to screen space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix or specific factorizations (e.g., shear-warp) [S2, S3, S4, unofficial].
For perspective projections, the kernel shape may be distorted (e.g., EWA splatting) to account for foreshortening [S6, unofficial][S10, unofficial].
Splatting compositing is performed along sheets (all pixels at once for a set of voxels), whereas ray-casting composites along rays (one sample at a time) [S10, unofficial].

The architecture was developed to address the performance bottlenecks of loading and storing large Gaussian splat clouds in JavaScript environments, leveraging Web Workers for asynchronous I/O and WebGL textures for GPU storage.
